features.title: Key grid with multitouch and rollover
features.description: Low-latency tap-to-type key grid that handles fast overlapping touches (rollover), cancelled touches and edge taps correctly. The rendering and hit-testing pipeline everything else builds on.
features.platformNotes: iOS keyboard extensions run under a tight memory ceiling, so renderer and Compose Multiplatform overhead must be measured early (see platform research).

features.title: Key press preview popup
features.description: Enlarged bubble showing the pressed character above the finger, with an option to disable it.
features.platformNotes: iOS: an extension cannot draw outside its own view, so top-row callouts need reserved headroom or an alternative design (verify).

features.title: Long-press alternate characters
features.description: Long-press (or swipe-up) on a key opens a popup of accented letters, symbols or digits defined per layout and locale.

features.title: Shift and caps lock
features.description: One-shot shift, double-tap (or gesture) caps lock, and correct shifted labels on all keys.

features.title: Auto-capitalization
features.description: Automatically shift at sentence starts and respect the text field's requested capitalization mode (words, sentences, characters, none).
features.platformNotes: Android: EditorInfo/getCursorCapsMode. iOS: autocapitalizationType trait plus documentContextBeforeInput, which only exposes limited context.

features.title: Field-aware layouts and action key
features.description: Adapt the layout to the field type (email '@' and '.com', URL, number, date/time, password) and label the action key from the field's IME action (Go, Search, Send, Next).
features.platformNotes: iOS: secure text fields and phone-pad fields always switch to the system keyboard, so a custom keyboard never sees them.

features.title: Haptic and sound feedback
features.description: Configurable vibration strength and key click sounds (optionally sound packs), respecting system silent or do-not-disturb state.
features.platformNotes: iOS: haptic (and per KeyboardKit docs, audio) feedback only works when the user grants Full Access.

features.title: Backspace repeat and word delete
features.description: Holding backspace auto-repeats and accelerates, optionally switching to whole-word deletion, without splitting composite emoji or grapheme clusters.

features.title: Symbol, number and numpad layers
features.description: Symbol and 'more symbols' pages plus a dedicated number pad shown automatically for numeric fields and reachable manually.

features.title: Optional number row
features.description: Persistent top row of digits, toggleable per user preference and shown automatically where layouts expect it.

features.title: Punctuation conveniences
features.description: Double-space inserts a period, auto-space after punctuation, and swapping a trailing space with punctuation typed next ('word ,' becomes 'word, ').

features.title: Probabilistic key hit correction
features.description: Resolve ambiguous taps with a spatial touch model combined with the language model (dynamic key targets), rather than fixed rectangular hit boxes.

features.title: Next-keyboard (globe) key
features.description: Key or long-press menu to switch to the next installed keyboard/input method.
features.platformNotes: iOS: must show a switch-keyboard key when needsInputModeSwitchKey is true (App Review expectation). Android: shouldOfferSwitchingToNextInputMethod.

features.title: Data-driven layout engine
features.description: Layouts, popups, and per-state key variants (shift, field type, RTL) defined in data files parsed by shared code instead of hard-coded views. Candidate formats: FlorisBoard-style JSON (also read by HeliBoard) or CLDR Keyboard 3.0 XML.
features.platformNotes: Pure shared logic and a good fit for commonMain.

features.title: Latin layout variants
features.description: QWERTY, QWERTZ, AZERTY plus alternative layouts (Dvorak, Colemak, Workman) selectable independently of the language.

features.title: Broad language coverage
features.description: Launch with a core set of languages (layout, long-press alternates, dictionary) and a data pipeline (e.g. CLDR exemplar characters) to scale to many more.

features.title: Fast language switching
features.description: Switch enabled languages/layouts via a language key, spacebar swipe or long-press menu, with the current language shown on the spacebar.

features.title: Multilingual typing
features.description: Type in two or more languages on one layout without switching, with suggestions and autocorrect drawn from all active dictionaries.

features.title: Right-to-left scripts
features.description: Arabic, Hebrew, Persian and other RTL layouts with mirrored function keys, correct bidi cursor movement and RTL-aware suggestion strip.

features.title: Tablet, landscape and foldable layouts
features.description: Layouts and scaling tuned for large screens, landscape and folded or unfolded states, remembered separately per posture.

features.title: Custom layout import
features.description: Users can paste or import a layout file (and edit key popups) in the app, with validation so broken layouts cannot crash the keyboard.

features.title: Visual layout editor
features.description: Graphical editor for creating and rearranging keys and popups without hand-writing layout files. In the open-source keyboards this exists mostly as community web tools.

features.title: CLDR Keyboard 3.0 (LDML) layouts
features.description: Read Unicode CLDR Keyboard 3.0 (UTS #35 Part 7) files so one standard source defines touch and hardware layouts for a language.
features.platformNotes: k3lp (Kotlin Multiplatform, Apache-2.0, pre-alpha) already parses Keyboard3 files and could be reused directly.

features.title: PC-style keys (Ctrl, Alt, Esc, Tab, F-keys)
features.description: Optional layout or row with modifier, Esc, Tab, arrow and function keys for terminals, SSH and remote desktops.
features.platformNotes: iOS: the text document proxy only inserts text, deletes and moves the cursor, so modifier combinations cannot reach the host app (verify).

features.title: Alternative input paradigms
features.description: Non-QWERTY paradigms such as 3x3 grids with swipe letters (MessagEase style), circular 8pen-style input, hexagonal layouts or T9 multi-tap for keypad phones.

features.title: Pluggable composition engine
features.description: An internal interface for composing input (dead keys, Hangul, Telex, kana, pinyin via librime) with preedit/composing text and candidate lists. This lets new scripts plug in without reworking the core.
features.platformNotes: Android supports composing regions natively. iOS uses setMarkedText on the proxy, which some host apps handle inconsistently (verify).

features.title: Dead keys and compose sequences
features.description: Dead keys and multi-key compose sequences for diacritics and rare characters.

features.title: Korean Hangul and Vietnamese Telex/VNI
features.description: Composition engines that assemble syllables from keystrokes: Hangul jamo composition and Vietnamese Telex/VNI tone-mark input.

features.title: Indic and complex-script input
features.description: Layouts and rules for Indic, Southeast Asian and other complex scripts (conjuncts, vowel signs, reordering), including phonetic or transliteration schemes that turn Latin keystrokes into native script.

features.title: Chinese input methods
features.description: Pinyin (full, fuzzy, double), Zhuyin, Wubi, Cangjie, stroke and Cantonese Jyutping with a candidate window and user phrase learning.
features.platformNotes: librime (BSD-3-Clause) already runs on Android (Trime, fcitx5, FUTO) and iOS (Hamster), so integrating it is far cheaper than building an engine.

features.title: Japanese kana-kanji input
features.description: Romaji and 12-key flick input with kana-kanji conversion and live conversion.
features.platformNotes: AzooKeyKanaKanjiConverter (MIT) is Swift-only, so it is reusable on iOS but not from shared Kotlin code.

features.title: Handwriting input
features.description: Draw characters on a canvas and have them recognized, mainly valuable for CJK and for users who cannot type.

features.title: Suggestion strip
features.description: Candidate bar with three or more suggestions (typed word, best guess, alternatives), punctuation shortcuts when idle, and case-aware suggestions that follow shift state.

features.title: Word completion
features.description: Frequency-ranked completion of the word being typed from a compact on-device dictionary (trie or DAWG), including diacritic-insensitive matching ('naive' finds 'naïve').
features.platformNotes: Shared engine in commonMain. Dictionary memory footprint is critical inside the iOS extension.

features.title: Autocorrect
features.description: Replace likely typos on space or punctuation using edit distance, keyboard proximity and word frequency, with adjustable aggressiveness and a per-language off switch.

features.title: One-tap autocorrect undo
features.description: Backspace immediately after an autocorrection restores the original word and stops correcting it again in the same spot.

features.title: Per-language dictionary packs
features.description: Bundled and importable dictionaries per language in a documented format, so languages can be added without an app update.
features.platformNotes: Offline-first Android keyboards have users download files in a browser and import them. On iOS, network access and a shared container both involve Full Access (see platform research). Wordlist licences vary per language.

features.title: Next-word prediction
features.description: Suggest likely next words after a space, using n-gram (bigram or trigram) statistics from the dictionary and the user's own history.
features.platformNotes: iOS provides no usable next-word API to extensions (KeyboardKit says Apple removed it in iOS 16), so MaKeeb must ship its own model.

features.title: On-device learning and forgetting
features.description: Learn new words and personal word pairs locally, and let users see, remove or reset learned data (for example long-press a suggestion to forget it).

features.title: Personal dictionary editor
features.description: View, add and delete user words (with an 'add to dictionary' action on the typed word) so names and jargon stop being autocorrected.
features.platformNotes: iOS: UILexicon exposes the user's system text replacements (read-only) to keyboards.

features.title: Text expansion shortcuts
features.description: User-defined abbreviations that expand into phrases ('omw' becomes 'On my way!'), offered as a suggestion or applied automatically.
features.platformNotes: iOS: Apple's text replacements can be imported through UILexicon.

features.title: Emoji suggestions
features.description: Offer matching emoji in the suggestion strip when a typed word matches an emoji name or keyword.

features.title: Password-manager inline autofill
features.description: Show password-manager and autofill chips inline in the suggestion strip or toolbar.
features.platformNotes: Android 11+ only (inline suggestions API). On iOS, AutoFill belongs to the system keyboard.

features.title: Suggestions when revisiting a word
features.description: Moving the cursor back into an earlier word shows its alternatives again, so a missed correction or wrong swipe can be fixed with one tap.
features.platformNotes: iOS: limited surrounding-text access makes this harder (verify).

features.title: System-wide spell checker service
features.description: Expose MaKeeb's dictionaries as the OS spell checker that underlines misspellings in any app.
features.platformNotes: Android-only (SpellCheckerService). iOS has no third-party spell-checker extension point.

features.title: Contact-name suggestions
features.description: Opt-in use of contact names as dictionary words so they are suggested and not autocorrected.
features.platformNotes: Android needs READ_CONTACTS, which is a privacy trade-off (LeanType removed it). iOS UILexicon may supply some contact names (verify).

features.title: Offensive-word filter
features.description: Keep offensive words out of suggestions and autocorrect targets by default. The user can still type them.

features.title: Glide / swipe typing
features.description: Enter whole words by sliding across letters, decoded against the dictionary and context, with a visible gesture trail, a floating preview, alternatives after each swipe, and learning of swiped words.
features.platformNotes: Reuse options: FUTO Swipe (GPL C++ library, models under the FUTO Model License, MIT dataset) or HeliBoard's NLnet-funded replacement library (planned Apache-2.0, unreleased). Decoding and trail rendering are shared logic.

features.title: Spacebar cursor slide
features.description: Slide horizontally on the spacebar to move the cursor character by character (optionally word by word).
features.platformNotes: iOS: adjustTextPosition(byCharacterOffset:) supports horizontal movement.

features.title: Trackpad cursor mode
features.description: Long-press the spacebar to turn the keyboard into a trackpad for two-dimensional cursor movement and selection.
features.platformNotes: iOS: the proxy only exposes character offsets, so vertical movement and selection must be approximated (verify).

features.title: Swipe-to-delete words
features.description: Swipe left from backspace to select a variable number of previous words and delete them on release.
features.platformNotes: iOS: word boundaries come from documentContextBeforeInput, which may be truncated.

features.title: Directional key swipes
features.description: Short swipes in up to eight directions on a key produce secondary characters or actions, so symbols can be reached without switching layers.

features.title: Configurable keyboard gestures
features.description: User-mappable gestures (swipe up, down, left or right on the keyboard or specific keys) for actions such as hide keyboard, shift, switch language or open the clipboard.

features.title: Toolbar / quick-action bar
features.description: Configurable row of actions (clipboard, emoji, settings, one-handed, select all, undo, incognito) that shares or alternates with the suggestion strip, with pinnable keys.

features.title: Cursor and navigation panel
features.description: Panel or layout with arrow keys, Home/End, word jumps and a select mode for precise editing.
features.platformNotes: iOS: only horizontal cursor moves are possible and extensions cannot create selections (verify).

features.title: Select, cut, copy and paste actions
features.description: One-tap Select All, Cut, Copy and Paste from the keyboard.
features.platformNotes: Android uses performContextMenuAction or key events. iOS: pasting needs Full Access to read the pasteboard, and cut/copy/select-all are largely unavailable to extensions (verify).

features.title: Undo / redo
features.description: Undo and redo keys that send the platform undo command to the focused app.
features.platformNotes: Android: Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z key events, which work only in some apps. iOS: no undo API for extensions (verify).

features.title: Emoji panel
features.description: Categorized, scrollable emoji picker with recents and a skin-tone/gender variant picker, reachable from a key or long-press.

features.title: Emoji search
features.description: Search emoji by name or keyword in the user's language, using CLDR annotations. Among the most-requested features in several open-source keyboards.
features.platformNotes: Needs text entry inside the keyboard itself (a search field that captures keystrokes), which both platforms allow.

features.title: Up-to-date emoji with compatibility
features.description: Keep emoji data current (Unicode 17 in 2026) while hiding or rendering emoji the device font cannot show.
features.platformNotes: Android: FUTO found the bundled emoji2 font adds about 9 MB and ships a trimmed 1 MB compatibility font instead. iOS: filter emoji by OS version.

features.title: Symbols and kaomoji panels
features.description: Extra panels for Unicode symbols (math, arrows, currency) and text emoticons or kaomoji.

features.title: GIF and sticker insertion
features.description: Search or browse GIFs and sticker packs (online or offline packs) and insert them into apps that accept rich content.
features.platformNotes: Android: commitContent works only in apps that support it. iOS: copy to the pasteboard and paste (Full Access). Online search needs network, which conflicts with an offline stance (FUTO declined GIF search for this reason).

features.title: Clipboard history
features.description: Local history of copied text with tap-to-paste, configurable retention and size, and an option for a private keyboard-internal clipboard.
features.platformNotes: Android 10+: only the focused default IME can read the clipboard. iOS: requires Full Access, and copies can only be captured while the keyboard is running (verify).

features.title: Pinned clips and snippets
features.description: Pin clips so they never expire, and keep a list of reusable snippets or quick texts.

features.title: Recent-copy paste suggestion
features.description: Show a freshly copied item as a one-tap chip in the suggestion strip for a short time.
features.platformNotes: iOS: requires Full Access.

features.title: Sensitive clip protection
features.description: Never store clips flagged as sensitive (for example passwords from managers), auto-expire unpinned items, and exclude clips copied in password fields.
features.platformNotes: Android 13+: ClipDescription EXTRA_IS_SENSITIVE.

features.title: Images and files in clipboard
features.description: Keep copied images, screenshots and files in history (with size caps) and paste them into apps that accept rich content.
features.platformNotes: Android: commitContent / content URIs. iOS: pasteboard only.

features.title: Clipboard search and filter
features.description: Search or filter clipboard history by text (optionally regex or tags).

features.title: Light/dark theme following the system
features.description: Built-in light and dark themes that follow the system setting, with optional time-based switching.

features.title: Material You dynamic color
features.description: Derive keyboard colors from the Android 12+ wallpaper palette.
features.platformNotes: Android 12+ only. iOS has no equivalent (could use the host's tint or the system accent).

features.title: Custom colors and theme editor
features.description: In-app editing of key, background, text and accent colors with a live preview.

features.title: Key borders, gaps, labels and hints
features.description: Toggle key borders, adjust corner radius and key gaps, key label and hint size, and show long-press hints on keys.

features.title: Background images and custom fonts
features.description: Use a photo or image as the keyboard background and choose custom key-label fonts.
features.platformNotes: iOS: importing a user photo happens in the containing app and needs the shared container to reach the extension.

features.title: Stylesheet-based theme engine
features.description: Declarative, element-level theme format (CSS-like selectors for keys, states, popups, toolbar) so artists can build complete themes beyond a color picker.
features.platformNotes: Shared engine in commonMain mapping to Compose styles on both platforms.

features.title: Theme import/export and gallery
features.description: Share themes as files and optionally browse a community gallery.

features.title: Per-app keyboard tint
features.description: Tint the keyboard to match the color of the app being typed into.
features.platformNotes: iOS: the host app identity and colors are not reliably available to extensions (verify).

features.title: Keyboard height and size
features.description: Adjust keyboard height, width and bottom offset, stored per orientation.
features.platformNotes: iOS: height is set with constraints on the input view, while width follows the screen (verify).

features.title: One-handed mode
features.description: Compact keyboard docked left or right with a quick toggle to switch sides.

features.title: Split keyboard
features.description: Split the layout into two halves for thumb typing on tablets, foldables and landscape phones.

features.title: Floating keyboard
features.description: Undocked, movable and resizable keyboard window, which is especially useful on tablets. Repeatedly requested in several open-source keyboards.
features.platformNotes: Android: feasible through IME window and insets handling (HeliBoard 4.0, FlorisBoard 0.6 alpha). iOS: floating is a system-keyboard feature and likely unavailable to extensions (verify).

features.title: Screen reader support
features.description: Full TalkBack/VoiceOver support: announced keys and suggestions, explore-by-touch with lift-to-type, and accessible panels.
features.platformNotes: Custom Compose-drawn keys need explicit semantics. Compose Multiplatform accessibility inside an Android IME window and an iOS extension needs early validation.

features.title: Font scale, contrast and reduced motion
features.description: Respect system font scaling without breaking layouts, offer high-contrast themes, and honor reduce-motion by disabling popups and animations.

features.title: Long-press and repeat timing
features.description: Adjustable long-press delay, key repeat rate and accidental-touch debounce for users with motor impairments.

features.title: Offline by design
features.description: Core keyboard needs no network access: no INTERNET permission on Android, and every core feature works without Full Access on iOS.
features.platformNotes: iOS: Full Access is all-or-nothing (network, pasteboard, haptics, shared container), so a clear 'what works without it' matrix is needed.

features.title: Incognito mode
features.description: Manual and automatic incognito that stops learning, history and emoji recents, turned on automatically when an app requests no personalized learning.
features.platformNotes: Android: IME_FLAG_NO_PERSONALIZED_LEARNING. iOS has no equivalent hint beyond secure fields (verify).

features.title: Password-field handling
features.description: In password fields, disable suggestions, learning, key previews and clipboard capture.
features.platformNotes: iOS: secure fields always use the system keyboard.

features.title: Lock-screen protection
features.description: When the device is locked, hide clipboard, suggestions and learned data, and handle direct-boot storage correctly.
features.platformNotes: Android direct boot: credential-protected storage is unavailable before the first unlock.

features.title: Encrypted local storage
features.description: Encrypt learned words and clipboard history at rest.
features.platformNotes: Android Keystore. iOS Keychain / Data Protection classes.

features.title: Reproducible builds and signing transparency
features.description: Reproducible Android builds and published signing-certificate hashes so users can verify binaries.
features.platformNotes: Android-only in practice. App Store binaries are re-signed by Apple.

features.title: Opt-in local data donation
features.description: Explicitly opt-in, user-reviewed export of anonymized typing or gesture samples to improve models, with blocklists and a review screen.

features.title: Voice input key
features.description: Microphone key that hands off to the system or an installed voice input method and returns afterwards.
features.platformNotes: iOS: keyboard extensions cannot use the microphone. KeyboardKit works around this by opening the containing app to record.

features.title: Built-in offline dictation
features.description: Speech-to-text built into the keyboard or a companion plugin, running fully on-device.
features.platformNotes: Android: RECORD_AUDIO inside the IME is allowed. iOS: only possible through a round-trip to the containing app.

features.title: Guided setup
features.description: First-run flow to enable and select the keyboard, explain permissions (Full Access on iOS), and pick languages.
features.platformNotes: iOS: users must add the keyboard in Settings manually, and a deep link can only open the app's settings page.

features.title: Settings app with in-keyboard quick settings
features.description: Companion app for all settings with search, plus a quick-settings panel reachable from the keyboard.
features.platformNotes: Shared Compose Multiplatform UI for both platforms.

features.title: Shared storage between app and keyboard
features.description: Settings, dictionaries and themes shared between the companion app and the keyboard process.
features.platformNotes: iOS: needs an App Group, and Apple's guide ties the shared container to Open Access, so a fallback is needed when Full Access is denied. Android: same app process, so this is trivial.

features.title: Backup and restore
features.description: Export and import settings, learned words, custom layouts, themes and clipboard pins as a file, with safe archive handling.
features.platformNotes: Validate archives on import (HeliBoard 4.0 fixed a backup-restore issue with manipulated zip files).

features.title: Cross-device sync
features.description: Sync settings, the personal dictionary and optionally the clipboard across devices, ideally through user-owned storage rather than a vendor account.
features.platformNotes: Conflicts with the offline stance. It could run in the containing app only (iCloud / Drive / WebDAV) without giving the keyboard network access.

features.title: Extension packages
features.description: Installable data packages bundling layouts, themes, dictionaries and emoji data (similar to FlorisBoard .flex or Keyman .kmp).
features.platformNotes: iOS forbids loading executable plugins, so packages must be data-only on both platforms for parity.

features.title: Automation and macros
features.description: Keys that run user macros or fire intents, and integration with automation apps.
features.platformNotes: Android-only in practice (intents, Tasker).

features.title: Hardware keyboard companion mode
features.description: When a physical keyboard is attached, hide the soft keys and keep only the suggestion or candidate bar (and CJK candidate window).
features.platformNotes: iOS: third-party keyboards get little or no hardware-key input (verify with platform research).

features.title: Hardware layout mapping and shortcuts
features.description: Map physical keys to the selected language layout (for example Cyrillic on a US keyboard) and support language-switch shortcuts such as Ctrl+Space.
features.platformNotes: Android: onKeyDown in InputMethodService. iOS: likely not feasible for extensions (verify).
